title: Experiment vs Control Cohort Definitions (Hosted API) — 2026 Q1
body:
Purpose
- Provide working cohort definitions for Hosted API pricing/packaging experiments in 2026 Q1.
- Ensure Product/RevOps/Finance use the same inclusion/exclusion criteria when comparing experiment vs control.
- Explicitly document known confounders (meter changes, model mix, caching, sales overlays) so readouts are interpretable.

Status / how to use
- This is a working doc. Changes must be called out in the weekly experiment review.
- When publishing a readout: copy the cohort definition block (incl. exclusions + confounders) into the readout so results are reproducible.

Glossary / fields (canonical names used in analysis datasets)
- account_id: internal customer/workspace identifier
- org_type: {self_serve, sales_led} (see definition)
- plan_tier: {free, builder, pro, enterprise} (internal naming; mapped in RevOps tables)
- first_paid_at: timestamp when account first became paid (if ever)
- first_usage_at: timestamp of first successful Hosted API usage event
- experiment_id: e.g., "2026q1_pkg_variant_b"
- variant: {control, treatment_a, treatment_b, ...}
- exposure_at: first timestamp where account was eligible + served a price/package experience
- is_eligible: boolean; rules vary per experiment
- usage_day: date in UTC (we will also compute local_day for customer exports; see confounders)
- billed_tokens_prompt / billed_tokens_completion / billed_tokens_total: post-meter-fix fields (preferred for billing-aligned analysis)
- raw_tokens_*: pre-meter-fix / engine-reported tokens (only for diagnostic comparisons)
- cache_hit_ratio: portion of tokens served from cache (if available; varies by timeframe)
- model_family: {llama, mistral, qwen, other}
- endpoint_type: {chat_completions, completions, embeddings, rerank}
- region: {us-east, us-west, eu-central, ...}

Primary cohort split: Self-serve vs Sales-led
Definition (Self-serve)
- Accounts that:
  - were acquired via PLG signup (no active opportunity at the time of first paid conversion), AND
  - have no assigned AE in HubSpot at exposure_at, AND
  - are on standard card/stripe billing (not invoiced terms) at exposure_at.
- Operational check: self_serve should represent accounts where packaging changes directly affect checkout and in-product upgrade.

Definition (Sales-led)
- Accounts that:
  - have an active opportunity within [-30d, +30d] of first_paid_at OR exposure_at (whichever earlier), OR
  - are on invoiced billing terms / order form pricing at exposure_at, OR
  - have an assigned AE and lifecycle_stage in {"opportunity", "negotiation", "legal", "closed_won"} at exposure_at.

Notes
- Some accounts transition: self-serve -> sales-led. We classify org_type at exposure_at (time of experiment exposure), not “today”.
- For accounts with mixed evidence (e.g., AE assigned but still on card): default to sales_led to avoid overstating PLG lift.

Secondary split: New vs Existing accounts
We need two “new/existing” concepts depending on the metric.

A) New for conversion metrics (recommended for signup-to-paid analysis)
- new_acct_conversion = accounts where exposure_at <= first_paid_at OR first_paid_at is null and exposure_at is within 14 days of first_usage_at.
- Intuition: accounts that are plausibly making their first purchase decision during the window.

B) Existing for retention / ARPU metrics (recommended for revenue and usage deltas)
- existing_acct_usage = accounts where first_paid_at < exposure_at - 30 days.
- Rationale: avoid mixing onboarding ramp with steady-state behavior.

Edge cases
- Re-activated accounts (churned then returned): treat as existing for usage, but tag separately as reactivated if last_paid_end_at exists and gap >= 60d.
- Accounts with first_paid_at missing due to billing system lag: use ledger_paid_event_at when available (Finance export).

Geography cohorts
We segment by both customer billing country and compute region-of-usage.

A) Customer billing country (stable attribute)
- geo_country = billing_country from CRM/billing profile (or tax country for self-serve).
- Primary rollups:
  - NA: US, CA
  - EU/UK: EU member states + UK + CH + NO
  - APAC: AU, NZ, SG, JP, KR, IN (and others as volume permits)
  - RoW

B) Usage region (variable attribute)
- usage_region = region dimension on usage events (preferred) aggregated by token-weighted majority region per account per week.
- Rule: if a single region accounts for >=70% of billed_tokens_total for the week, assign that region; else label "multi-region".

Why both?
- Pricing and margin are driven by usage_region (COGS), while GTM motion and legal/tax constraints correlate more with geo_country.

Model mix cohorts
We need model-mix segmentation because pricing experiments often shift customers across models and sequence lengths.

Model mix definitions (token-weighted)
- For each account-week, compute share of billed_tokens_total by model_family and by model_id.
- Primary categories:
  1) "frontier-open-large": top-tier larger open models (internal list maintained by PM; update quarterly)
  2) "mid": mid-size general models
  3) "small-fast": small/latency-optimized models
  4) "embeddings-heavy": embeddings tokens/units dominate

Simple assignment rule
- If embeddings endpoint accounts for >=60% of total billable units (tokens-equivalent) -> embeddings-heavy.
- Else assign the model category with highest share of billed_tokens_total.

Important note
- Do not use request_count alone for mix; streaming and long-context usage distort request-weighted mix.

Experiment exposure: who is “in experiment” vs control
We distinguish eligibility, exposure, and analysis population.

Eligibility (is_eligible)
- Must satisfy experiment-specific rules (e.g., self-serve only, NA only, new accounts only).
- Must have at least 1 successful Hosted API request (2xx) within the 7 days before exposure_at OR within the first 48 hours after exposure_at.
  - Purpose: exclude drive-by signups that never truly enter the product.

Exposure (exposure_at)
- exposure_at is the first time the account is served the experiment experience (pricing page, checkout, upgrade modal, or API-side plan enforcement message depending on experiment).
- If instrumentation is missing for an account, do not infer exposure from plan_tier changes alone (can be confounded by manual overrides).

Control assignment
- Control = eligible accounts not exposed to treatment and explicitly flagged as control in the experiment assignment table.
- If experiment uses rollout by hash bucket: control are buckets not receiving treatment.

Treatment assignment
- Treatment = eligible accounts exposed to variant != control.

Unit of randomization
- Default: account_id (workspace).
- If the experiment is per-project/api_key: we must roll up to account_id for revenue metrics and treat project-level exposure as a nested attribute; otherwise contamination is likely.

Exclusion rules (global)
Exclude accounts/usage from the primary analysis population if any of the following apply:
1) Manual price overrides / custom contracts at exposure_at
- Reason: their realized prices are not governed by the experiment.
- Operationalization: invoiced terms OR discount_percent >= 30% OR non-standard rate card id.

2) Support remediation windows
- If account received a billing credit for metering disputes during the window, tag "credit_adjusted" and exclude from revenue lift but include in qualitative notes.

3) Internal / test accounts
- Redwood-owned domains, load-test accounts, perf-canary, integration test tenants.

4) Meter-definition transition overlap (see next section)
- When meter changes affect billed_tokens fields, segment pre/post and exclude ambiguous overlap windows for certain analyses.

5) Abuse / anomalous traffic
- Accounts flagged by Trust/Safety or with extreme outliers:
  - billed_tokens_total > P99.9 AND request success rate < 70% (often retry storms)
  - Note: keep a separate “outlier appendix” for Finance review; do not silently drop without a note.

Key confounders (must be stated in any readout)
1) Meter fixes overlapping experiment windows
- We have active work on:
  - double-counting on retry/fallback paths (streaming especially)
  - embeddings batched metering correctness
  - missing region dimension
  - cache-hit attribution fields
- Requirement: all analyses must include a pre/post segmentation keyed by meter_change_effective_at (per PR rollout notes).
- If the experiment starts before the meter fix but ends after, do NOT compute a single pooled lift number without controlling for the change.

2) Caching and cache-hit attribution maturity
- Cache-hit fields may be missing or backfilled for some date ranges.
- Impact: treatment that changes caching configuration (directly or indirectly via model choice) can appear as margin improvements unrelated to pricing.

3) Model routing / fallback events
- Capacity events can route traffic to compatible model variants.
- Pricing experiments that change demand can change fallback frequency (affects both cost and perceived quality).
- We should track fallback_rate per cohort-week if available.

4) Sales overlays / negotiated discounts
- Even “self-serve” can receive ad-hoc credits from Support or Growth.
- We need a “promo_credit_applied” flag per billing cycle to avoid attributing revenue changes to packaging.

5) Seasonality / product launches
- New SDK releases and major model launches can change baseline conversion and usage.
- Add a timeline annotation in readouts for major releases impacting onboarding funnel.

Recommended cohort tables for standard readouts
Use these as defaults to reduce “analysis drift” across readouts.

Table 1: Conversion (new accounts only)
- Population: self_serve AND new_acct_conversion AND eligible
- Compare: control vs treatment
- Metric windows:
  - D0–D7 paid conversion
  - D0–D14 paid conversion
  - Time-to-upgrade median

Table 2: Retention / usage (existing paid accounts)
- Population: existing_acct_usage AND paid at exposure_at
- Compare: control vs treatment
- Metric windows:
  - Week 1–4 usage (billed_tokens_total)
  - Logo retention at day 30
  - GRR proxy: revenue in days 1–30 vs baseline 30d pre

Table 3: Margin (usage_region + model mix)
- Population: paid accounts with stable metering fields post-fix
- Compare: control vs treatment
- Metrics:
  - gross_margin_pct (from FP&A model)
  - cost per 1M billed tokens (by region)
  - cache_hit_ratio and batching indicators (if available)

Implementation notes / pseudo-SQL (illustrative)
- Cohort assignment should be implemented in a single versioned model so Finance/RevOps/Prod use the same output.

Pseudo-logic:
- org_type = case
  when invoiced_terms_at(exposure_at)=true then 'sales_led'
  when ae_assigned_at(exposure_at)=true and lifecycle_stage_at(exposure_at) in ('opportunity','negotiation','legal','closed_won') then 'sales_led'
  when opportunity_active_between(exposure_at-30d, exposure_at+30d)=true then 'sales_led'
  else 'self_serve' end

- existing_acct_usage = (first_paid_at is not null) and (first_paid_at < exposure_at - interval '30 days')
- new_acct_conversion = (first_paid_at is null) or (first_paid_at >= exposure_at - interval '3 days')
  (NOTE: exact thresholds to be finalized per experiment; above is a working default)

Data quality checks (minimum)
- Verify variant assignment is stable per account_id (no flips). If flips occur, exclude account and log count by day.
- Verify region is non-null for >= 99.5% of billed_tokens_total post-region-fix.
- Verify billed_tokens_total >= raw_tokens_total * 0.95 and <= raw_tokens_total * 1.05 in stable periods (diagnostic only; exceptions expected with retries/cache fields).

Open questions / TODO
1) Final definition of “active opportunity” window
- Current proposal: [-30d, +30d] around exposure_at or first_paid_at. Need RevOps sign-off.

2) Should we classify “invoice-on-Stripe” (monthly invoicing but still self-serve motion) as sales_led?
- Jordan suggests yes for pricing experiments; Nikhil suggests create a third group: "hybrid".

3) Meter-change calendar
- Need a single source-of-truth table of meter_change_effective_at by endpoint and region.
- Logan/Nadia to provide; Chris to integrate into analysis templates.

4) Timezone alignment for daily cohorts
- We use UTC usage_day for consistency, but some experiments reference daily exports in customer local time.
- Proposal: keep UTC for primary; add local_day only for customer-case deep dives.

Change log
- 2026-02-22: Added explicit exclusions for credit_adjusted accounts; clarified sales-led classification precedence.
- 2026-02-12: Added meter-change overlap requirement (pre/post segmentation) per Product thread; added model mix cohorts.
- 2026-01-14: Initial draft.
